payload.title: What Are the Baltic Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
protect_keywords: baltic wedding traditions you never knew (old URL; SEO to quantify US and AU)
payload.audience: Couples in their 30s interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, AUD 150k+ budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s with a generous budget, often with a Latvian-, Lithuanian- or Estonian-Australian partner or parent, who want to know which customs belong to which of the three countries (not a blended 'Baltic' list), what each looks like on the day, and whether to marry in Riga, Vilnius or Tallinn (Smartraveller: exercise normal safety precautions in all three, with a higher level near Latvia's border with Belarus) or carry the customs into a wedding at home.
payload.goal: Read the free Wedded Wonderland digital magazine (primary CTA); secondary, in-context invitation to speak with a Wedded Advisor placed after the 'for Australians' section.
payload.angle: Most 'Baltic wedding' lists blend three countries into one and invent the rest (top hats, canopies, six-month engagements). Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania each have their own language and customs, so we say that once and then tie every custom to the country its source names: Latvia's mičošana and playful bride-stealing, Lithuania's matchmaker, wreath removal, bread-and-salt welcome and dowry chest, Estonia's bonnet ceremony and the wedding traditions UNESCO records on Kihnu and among the Seto. We use UNESCO, national museums and official tourism sites, label the rest 'often told', correct the old myths, and give Australian couples the practical layer the top results skip: Smartraveller levels for each country, which Australian embassy covers it (Stockholm for Estonia and Latvia, Warsaw for Lithuania), and the CNI and recognition steps as at November 2026.
must_include: One early framing line: Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania each have their own language, customs and law; customs below are tied to the country the source names, and vary by region and family
Customs grouped by country (Latvia, Lithuania, Estonia), each numbered, about 10 in total, with the country named in or beside each heading
Latvian mičošana and the Lithuanian and Estonian headdress customs explained as separate, country-specific rites
UNESCO elements quoted only as far as their own text links them to weddings (Kihnu 2008, Seto leelo 2009, Suiti 2009, sutartinės 2010, Baltic Song and Dance Celebrations 2008)
Myth corrections from the old page (top hat, canopy, six-month 'legally binding' engagement, veil passed to a sister) in one honest short note, no reused wording

Section for Australians: Smartraveller level and update date for each country (as at November 2026), Latvia's higher-level Belarus border areas, Australian Embassy Stockholm (Estonia, Latvia) and Warsaw (Lithuania) for CNI and notarial, 'Getting married overseas' for recognition, registry 'check with the registry and the embassy, including any fees'; Baltic-Australian weddings at home
FAQ of 5 to 7 questions with no amounts

tradition_plan.note: Planner (wedding-planner-sme) runs batch A and batch B in parallel, scratch folders 02-research/batch-a and 02-research/batch-b, 15 min HARD by the clock, save after every 3 facts, no extra sourcing rounds. Preferred sources: ich.unesco.org element pages, national museums (Latvian National Museum of History lnvm.lv, Latvian Ethnographic Open-Air Museum brivdabasmuzejs.lv, Lithuanian National Museum lnm.lt, Open-Air Museum of Lithuania llbm.lt, Estonian National Museum erm.ee, Estonian Open Air Museum evm.ee), culture ministries, visitestonia.com, latvia.travel, lithuania.travel, latvia.eu, lithuania.lt, estonica.org, Britannica, academic journals. Never competitor wedding sites, vendor blogs, Wikipedia, lifestyle magazines. Unsourced: 'often told', no meanings as fact, no [[VERIFY]] marker. Terms with diacritics as the source gives them. Every custom tied to its country; nothing pan-Baltic unless a source says so. One honest framing line per section. Culture, not politics.
tradition_plan.count: 10 customs plus optional item 7b plus UNESCO checks plus the legal section (batch A: 7 Latvia and Lithuania customs plus optional 7b; batch B: 3 Estonia customs, UNESCO checks, legal)

batch_B.tradition: For Australians: marrying in the Baltics, or bringing the customs home
facts_to_source: Smartraveller (read 2026-11-05): Estonia 'Exercise normal safety precautions', updated 29 October 2026; Latvia 'Exercise normal safety precautions overall' with 'Reconsider your need to travel' to areas near the border with Belarus, updated 02 June 2026; Lithuania 'Exercise normal safety precautions', updated 14 April 2026; all still current at 06 November 2026. Australian Embassy, Stockholm (sweden.embassy.gov.au) covers Estonia and Latvia for full consular and notarial services; local consulates in Tallinn and Riga give limited help.
